Rashi on Pesachim 50a:10:1.hebrew: עד שעה שהסוס רץ ומציל - כשיעור מרוצת הסוס עד חצי היום. ולשון מציל — שצילו תחתיו, שכל שעות היום חמה נוטה לצדדין וצל האדם וצל הבהמה נוטה לצידו; כשחמה במזרח, צל האדם למערב. אבל בחצי היום, חמה עומדת באמצע הרקיע בראש כל האדם, וצל הסוס תחתיו. בפי' ר' מכיר זצ"ל מצאתי:
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:10:1.english: Until the hour that the horse runs and casts a shadow [metzeil] - [That is,] the distance of a horse's run until midday. And the expression metzeil [means] that its shadow is beneath it, for during all [other] hours of the day the sun inclines to the sides, and a person's shadow and an animal's shadow incline to its side; when the sun is in the east, a person's shadow is to the west. But at midday, the sun stands in the middle of the firmament, above every person's head, and the horse's shadow is beneath it. I found [this] in the commentary of Rabbi Makhir, of blessed memory.

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:11:1.hebrew: כל מצילות - כלומר, שתולין לסוס לנוי ולקשקש, לשון מצלתים (ד"ה א יג):
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:11:1.english: All bells [metzillot] - That is to say, [bells] that they hang on a horse for adornment and to jingle, [from] the expression metziltayim [cymbals] (I Chronicles 13).

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:11:2.english: [It] will be holy to the Lord - For Israel will donate their freewill offerings to the Temple.

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:13:1.hebrew: כל ביזה שיבוזו ישראל - מן הנכרים ביום אחד עד חצות, יהיו קודש לה', שיביאום נדבה למקדש:
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:13:1.english: All spoils that Israel will take - from the gentiles in one day until midday will be sacred to God, [in] that they will bring them as a donation to the Temple.

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:13:2.hebrew: הסירות כמזרקים - אף הסירות יהיו של כסף ושל זהב, שתהא שם ביזה רבה להקדש:
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:13:2.english: The pots [shall be] like the basins - Even the pots will be of silver and of gold, for there will be abundant spoil there for the Temple treasury.

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:13:3.english: What [is the meaning of] “And the pots [shall be] like the basins” - For on the bells of the horse there is not so much consecrated [wealth].

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:13:4.hebrew: דמיתעתרי ישראל - יתעשרו ישראל, ובשורה אחרת היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:13:4.english: That Israel will become wealthy - Israel will become wealthy, and it is another good tiding.

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:14:1.hebrew: כנעני - לא יהיו צריכין גזברין לעשות סחורה בנכסי הקדש, לפי שיהא שם עושר גדול מן הביזה:
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:14:1.english: A merchant - [the Temple] treasurers will not need to engage in commerce with consecrated property, because there will be great wealth there from the spoils.

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:15:1.hebrew: בא אברהם והזהיר את יצחק - שהשביע לאליעזר, "לא תקח אשה לבני מבנות הכנעני" (בראשית כ״ד:ג׳):
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:15:1.english: Abraham came and warned Isaac - For he made Eliezer swear, "You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites" (Genesis 24:3).

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:15:2.hebrew: ויצחק את יעקב - "לא תקח אשה מבנות כנען" (שם כח):
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:15:2.english: And Isaac [warned] Jacob - "You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan" (Genesis 28:1).

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:17:1.english: All of it [is] “Who is good and does good” - For there are no bad tidings there.

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:1:1.hebrew: כאיסורו - של חמץ, ובשר קודש נמי משנפסל ביוצא אסור באכילה:
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:1:1.english: Like its prohibition - [That] of chametz; and sacrificial meat as well, once it becomes disqualified by going out [beyond its boundary], is forbidden to be eaten.

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:20:1.hebrew: למידרשיה בפירקא - קרייה דיו"ד ה"י דארבע אותיות, דרשיה וטעמיה התלויים בו:
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:20:1.english: To expound it in the public lecture - The reading of [the Name] Yod-He of four letters, its exposition and its reasons that depend upon it.

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:20:2.hebrew: לעלם כתיב - "זה שמי לעלם", חסר וי"ו, לשון העלמה:
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:20:2.english: Le'alem is written - "This is My name forever [le'olam]" [is written] without a vav, [which is] an expression of concealment.

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:21:1.hebrew: כתיב זה שמי לעלם - בהעלמה, וכתיב זה זכרי, דמשמע קרייה ולא העלמה. לשון אחר: כיון דכתב זה שמי, פשיטא דזה זכרי, היאך יקרא אלא בשמו:
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:21:1.english: It is written: "This is My name forever [le'olam]" - [That is,] in concealment [beha'alamah], and it is written "This is My memorial," which implies pronouncing [it] and not concealment. Another explanation: Since it wrote "This is My name," it is obvious that "This is My memorial" [is also so, for] how [else] would He be called except by His name?

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:21:2.hebrew: לא כשאני נכתב - שני שמות לימדו: שם הכתיבה ושם הקרייה:
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:21:2.english: Not as I am written - [God] taught him two names: the written name and the pronounced name.

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:23:1.english: Until midday - Half of the day.

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:23:2.hebrew: שלא לעשות - כדי שלא יהא טרוד במלאכה וישכח ביעור חמצו ושחיטת הפסח ותקון מצה לצורך הלילה, דמצוה לטרוח מבעוד יום כדי להסב מהר, כדאמר בפרק בתרא (דף קט:): חוטפין מצה בלילי פסחים בשביל תינוקות שלא ישנו:
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:23:2.english: Not to perform [labor] - So that he will not be preoccupied with labor and forget the removal of his leaven, the slaughtering of the Passover offering, and the preparation of matzah for the needs of the night; for it is a mitzvah to exert oneself while it is still day in order to recline promptly [at the Seder], as it says in the last chapter (109b): "We snatch matzah on Passover nights for the sake of the children, so that they do not fall asleep."

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:3:1.hebrew: יקרות וקפאון - איידי דאיירי בירושלים ביציאות שעריה, דקתני וכן מי שיצא מירושלים כו', פתח בהא פרשתא, דבעינן למימר קמן שעתיד הקב"ה להוסיף על ירושלים:
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:3:1.english: Yekarot vekippaon - Since [the Gemara] was dealing with Jerusalem regarding leaving its gates — as it teaches, "And similarly, one who went out from Jerusalem, etc." — it opened with this passage, because we are going to state further on that the Holy One, Blessed be He, will in the future expand Jerusalem.

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:4:1.hebrew: אור שיקר בעולם הזה - כשחמה מאירה בגבורתה ואורה גדול, אותו אור חשוב ויקר שלה יהא קפוי וקל לעולם הבא. כל דבר קל קרי קפוי, צף על המים; "ויצף הברזל" מתרגמינן: "וקפא פרזלא" (מלכים ב ו׳:ו׳):
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:4:1.english: Light that is precious in this world - When the sun shines in its full strength and its light is great, that significant and precious light of its will be kafuy and light in the World-to-Come. Any light thing is called kafuy, [as in something that] floats on water; "and the iron floated" (II Kings 6:6) is translated [into Aramaic] as "and the iron floated" (ukefa parzela).

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:6:1.english: People who are esteemed - Wealthy and important, but they are not good to the Omnipresent.

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:6:2.english: He expired - He expired and his spirit departed.

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:6:3.english: Those above [were] below - Those who were important here, I saw [as] insignificant.

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:6:4.english: And we - [i.e.,] Torah scholars, how are we there?

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:8:1.english: Martyred by the government and nothing more - Did they have no other merit for which they would be esteemed, except this alone?

Rashi on Pesachim 50a:8:2.hebrew: הרוגי לוד - שני אחים היו שמסרו עצמן על ישראל, שהודו על עצמן הריגת בת מלך שהיו מטילין אותה על כל ישראל:
Rashi on Pesachim 50a:8:2.english: The martyrs of Lod - They were two brothers who gave themselves up for Israel, for they confessed to [having committed] the murder of the king's daughter, which [the authorities] were blaming on all of Israel.

Tosafot on Pesachim 50a:23:1.hebrew: מקום שנהגו - אור"י בשם ריב"א דמפרש בירושלמי: מאי שנא ערבי פסחים משאר י"ט? משום דזמן הפסח מחצות ואילך. ואף יחיד, קאמר התם, בשאר ימות השנה ביום שמביא קרבן אסור במלאכה. ופריך: אם כן יהא כל היום אסור, כמו יחיד שמביא קרבן! ומפרש התם: משום דראוי להקריב משחרית, אבל פסח אינו יכול להקריבו אלא אחר חצות, כדנפקא לן מ"בין הערבים". ופריך: אם כן, קרבן תמיד שהוא לכל ישראל וקרב בכל יום — יהא בכל יום אסור במלאכה! ומשני: שאני תמיד, שהתורה הוציאה מן הכלל, דכתיב "ואספת דגנך", ואם כל ישראל יושבים ובטלים — מי יאסוף להן דגן? ומשמע התם דמדאורייתא אסורה. ונראה דאף בזמן הזה דליכא הקרבה, כיון שנאסר אז — אסור לעולם:
Tosafot on Pesachim 50a:23:1.english: A place where they were accustomed - R"I says in the name of Riba that it is explained in the Jerusalem Talmud: What is different about the eves of Passover compared to other festivals? Because the time of the Paschal offering is from midday onward. And even an individual, it says there, on other days of the year, on the day that he brings a sacrifice, is forbidden [to perform] labor. And [the Jerusalem Talmud] asks: If so, let the entire day be forbidden, like an individual who brings a sacrifice! And it explains there: Because [an individual's sacrifice] is fit to be offered from the morning, whereas a Paschal offering one can only offer after midday, as we derive from "between the evenings." And it asks: If so, the daily offering, which is for all of Israel and is offered every day — let every day be forbidden in labor! And it answers: The daily offering is different, for the Torah excluded it from the general rule, as it is written, "and you shall gather in your grain," and if all of Israel sit idle, who will gather grain for them? And it is implied there that by Torah law [labor] is forbidden. And it appears that even nowadays, when there is no offering, since it was forbidden then, it is forbidden forever:
